english.title: Wholesaler fail to record the transaction and disposal of a veterinary medicinal product
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the holder of a wholesale dealer's authorisation, failed to record as soon as reasonably practicable, after an

(A)_[incoming]_
(B)_[outgoing]_

transaction relating to a veterinary medicinal product, namely **(..SPECIFY PRODUCT..), the

(C)_[date and nature of the transaction]_
(D)_[name of the veterinary medicinal product]_
(E)_[manufacturer's batch number]_
(F)_[expiry date]_
(G)_[quantity]_
(H)_[name and address of the supplier]_
(I)_[name and address of the recipient]_
(J)_[**(..WHERE MORE THAN ONE OF THE ABOVE APPLIES - SPECIFY..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 22, 43(n) and 44(1) of the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013.

english.notes: From the 17th May 2024, this offence no longer applies due to changes made by the Veterinary Medicines (Amendment etc.) Regulations 2024. For the offence applying from that date, see H101681.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
